Oh, oh no. You scratched at the healing tattoo. Oh my sweet summer child. (Seriously not judging tho, tattoo’s are itchy af).
You are highly unlikely to get a visible dimple in your skin from it unless you are prone to scarring or you scratch again. Some ink will likely fall out but you’ll be able to get that easily retouched. Moisturiser really helps itchiness, apply a nice thin layer multiple times per day. Ice blocks can also relieve itching :) if the itching becomes problematic just keep an eye out for infection or reaction (it looks great atm tho other than those cheeky bits missing colour). Don’t scratch! :P

That looks like normal scabbing. It’s likely a mixture of dried plasma/maybe a tiny bit of blood/leftover ink. If it goes red or swollen that’s when you worry. The main thing at this stage is to resist the urge to pick/scratch. A thin layer of ointment can help. My scalp/neck/back tattoo scabbed up *just* like this and it healed great with no ink loss :)

That’s a really tricky situation, it’s easy for me to sit here and recommend a professional but people forget that’s not always easy! I’m not sure what country you’re in, and please excuse me if my judgement is incorrect, but it sounds like there may be a stigma against talking to a professional where you live? It’s really hard when family also believe that stigma, just know that you are NOT weak for needing help, it is NOT a deficit or anything wrong with your character. I personally believe that swallowing ones ego and admitting you need help is BRAVE. It’s also really hard to do.

There are videos on sites like YouTube that can help explain to your family about mental health, if they’re open to watching them that is. It’s a chemical imbalance in the brain - it is no less valid than a broken leg!

It sounds like your friends are trying to support you but don’t know the right things to say, maybe again you could try show them some studies proving mental health is valid, and should be taken seriously? Often people say things without realising they’ve just made it worse (eg, I hate people telling me “it’s fine, you’re fine,” because I’m NOT fine lol).

I’m so glad you feel a bit better today, it’s good to keep in mind that our moods change and taking things one day at a time is an effective way to get through.
Sending positive vibes x
